They used sticks and clubs instead, and while he was standing there, I don't know what they used, but they beat him until his face was broken in two places. We heard that the aunt <note>referring to Wang Xifeng</note> has a type of medicine for wounds from sticks; could you, Miss, find a pill for me?"

Baochai heard this and hurriedly ordered Ying'er to find two pills to give to Ping'er. Baochai said, "Since that is the case, you go and offer my regards on my behalf; I will not go myself." Ping'er promised Baochai and left. There is no need to speak further of this.

To return to Xiangling, after seeing the others and finishing supper, she saw that Baochai and the rest had gone to the mother's place, so she went to the Xiaoxiang Pavilion. By this time, Daiyu had mostly recovered, and seeing that Xiangling had also moved into the Garden to live, she was naturally pleased. Xiangling laughed and said, "Now that I have finally moved in and have some free time, if you would teach me to write poetry, that would be my great good fortune!" Daiyu laughed and said, "If you want to learn to write poetry, you must take me as your teacher. Although I am not a master, I can certainly teach you the basics." Xiangling laughed and said, "If it is really like that, I will take you as my teacher, but you must not get annoyed with me." Daiyu said, "What is so difficult that it is worth fretting over? It is nothing more than the <term>qi-cheng-zhuan-he</term> <gloss>the four-part structure of classical poetry: introduction, development, transition, and conclusion</gloss>. The middle development and transition sections consist of two pairs of couplets: matching level tones with oblique tones, and empty words with solid words. If you have truly brilliant lines, even if the tones and the matching of empty and solid words are not perfect, you can still use them."

Xiangling laughed, "No wonder whenever I would get hold of an old book of poetry and read a few pieces, some were matched perfectly, while others were not. I also heard people say, 'The first, third, and fifth characters do not matter, but the second, fourth, and sixth must be precise,' yet when I looked at the poetry of the ancients, some followed this, while others had errors in the second, fourth, and sixth positions. That is why I have been puzzled every day. Now that I hear you say this, it turns out these rules are not really matters of concern; it is most important that the words and phrases are fresh and unconventional." Daiyu said, "That is exactly the principle. Words and phrases are actually secondary. The most important thing is the concept. If the sentiment is genuine, even the words do not need much refinement to be good. This is what is called 'not letting the words harm the meaning.'"

Xiangling said, "I only love the lines by Lu Fangweng <note>Lu You, a famous Southern Song dynasty poet</note>: 'The heavy curtains are not rolled up, the scent remains long; the ancient inkstone is slightly concave, gathering much ink.' They are so vivid and interesting!" Daiyu said, "Because you all do not know poetry, you only love these shallow and easy ones. Once you enter that pattern, you will never be able to learn properly. Just listen to me: if you truly want to learn, I have the <term>Wang Mojie Quanji</term> <gloss>Complete Works of Wang Wei</gloss> here. You should first carefully ponder and memorize his hundred five-character regulated verses. After that, read the hundred and twenty seven-character regulated verses of Old Du <note>Du Fu</note>, and after that, read one or two hundred seven-character quatrains by Li Qinglian <note>Li Bai</note>. Once you have these three masters as your foundation in your belly, then look at the works of Tao Yuanming, Ying, Liu, Xie, Ruan, Yu, and Bao <note>poets of the Wei, Jin, and Northern and Southern Dynasties</note>. Since you are such an extremely clever and bright person, in less than a year, I have no doubt you will be a poet." Xiangling listened and laughed, "If that is the case, good Miss, take that book out for me; I will take it back, and it will be good to recite a few poems at night." Daiyu heard this and ordered Zijuan to bring the five-character regulated verses of Wang Youcheng <note>Wang Wei</note> and hand them to Xiangling, saying, "Only look at those with red circles; they are all my selections. Read them one by one. If you do not understand anything, ask your maid, or when you meet me, I will explain it to you."

Xiangling took the poems and returned to the Hengwu Courtyard. Ignoring all other matters, she sat under the lamp and read them one by one. Baochai urged her several times to sleep, but she would not. Seeing her such painstaking effort, Baochai had no choice but to let her be.

One day, after Daiyu had just finished washing and combing her hair, she saw Xiangling humming to herself as she brought the book back, wanting to exchange it for Du's regulated verses. Daiyu laughed and asked, "How many have you memorized in total?" Xiangling laughed, "I have read all of those selected with red circles." Daiyu said, "Have you gained any understanding?" Xiangling laughed, "I have gained some, but I don't know if it is correct. Let me tell you what I think."

<summary>Daiyu instructs Xiangling on the principles of poetry, emphasizing that authentic sentiment is more important than strict adherence to tonal rules, and provides her with classic collections to study.</summary>
<keywords>Xiangling, Daiyu, poetry, Wang Wei, Du Fu, Li Bai, literary study</keywords>
